messages.title: The Read Succeeded. Is It Fresh Enough?
messages.subtitle: A successful response can still be too old for this caller. Carry the committed revision into the read contract.
messages.property: A Product42 read that requests minimum revision R must not return a state below R.
messages.takeaway: A read is fresh enough only relative to a stated requirement. A successful write can provide the next read's concrete lower-bound revision.
messages.step.write-success.title: The price update commits
messages.step.write-success.lead: Product42 starts at revision 43 with price 100. The authoritative store commits price 120 at revision 44.
messages.step.revision-token.title: The caller receives revision 44
messages.step.revision-token.lead: The write response includes committed revision 44. That token is evidence the caller can carry into a verification read.
messages.step.http-200.title: The next read returns HTTP 200
messages.step.http-200.lead: The immediate verification request succeeds at the transport layer. What state did the read actually observe?
messages.step.projection-behind.title: The projection still has 43
messages.step.projection-behind.lead: The asynchronous projection returns revision 43 and price 100. It has not yet applied the committed revision 44.
messages.step.transport-question.title: Did the request succeed?
messages.step.transport-question.lead: Yes: the API returned HTTP 200 and a valid projected record. That only answers the transport and ordinary-read question.
messages.step.freshness-question.title: Did verification succeed?
messages.step.freshness-question.lead: No: this caller needs at least revision 44, but received 43. The response is valid data under a weaker contract and too old for this workflow.
messages.step.separate.title: Separate success from freshness
messages.step.separate.lead: HTTP 200 says the read completed. It does not say the returned revision meets a caller-specific minimum.
messages.step.property.title: State the lower-bound property
messages.step.property.lead: If the request specifies minimum revision R, a successful result for Product42 must have revision at least R. Here R is 44.
messages.step.sleep.title: Why not sleep first?
messages.step.sleep.lead: A fixed delay gives no evidence that projection revision 44 has arrived unless the system promises a bounded propagation time.
messages.step.value-poll.title: Why not poll for price 120?
messages.step.value-poll.lead: Revision 45 might legitimately change the price to 125. Waiting for exactly 120 can reject a result that is newer than the required revision 44.
messages.step.minimum-revision.title: Put the requirement in the read
messages.step.minimum-revision.lead: GetProduct(Product42, minimumRevision=44) must either return revision 44 or higher, or clearly decline the fresh-enough claim.
messages.step.reject-43.title: Revision 43 cannot satisfy 44
messages.step.reject-43.lead: With required 44 and projected 43, return NOT_FRESH_ENOUGH, wait for catch-up, or use an authoritative fallback. Do not report 43 as a successful fresh-enough result.
messages.step.catch-up.title: The projection catches up
messages.step.catch-up.lead: The projection applies revision 44 with price 120. A later verification read can now satisfy the same minimum.
messages.step.positive-44.title: Revision 44 satisfies 44
messages.step.positive-44.lead: Required 44, projected 44: the projection meets the lower bound and may return price 120.
messages.step.positive-45.title: Revision 45 also satisfies 44
messages.step.positive-45.lead: Required 44, projected 45: the newer record also qualifies, even if its price is 125. The API does not promise an exact revision or exact value.
messages.step.eventual-control.title: A weaker workflow can accept 43
messages.step.eventual-control.lead: A public browsing read with an explicit eventual-read contract and no minimum revision may legitimately return projected revision 43.
messages.step.lost-token.title: What if the caller loses the token?
messages.step.lost-token.lead: If the caller discards committed revision 44, a later read may have no evidence that this workflow requires at least 44.
messages.step.cache.title: The cache must honor the bound too
messages.step.cache.lead: A cache that returns revision 43 can break the guarantee even if a deeper projection has reached 44. The minimum must apply end to end.
messages.step.remaining.title: At least 44 is not absolute latest
messages.step.remaining.lead: Revision 44 satisfies this request even if the source has already committed 45. The lower bound does not promise the globally latest state.
messages.step.transfer.title: Transfer: confirm a profile change
messages.step.transfer.lead: A profile update returns revision 81; the confirmation projection has 80. Which evidence decides whether the confirmation read is fresh enough? Would 82 qualify?
messages.step.recap.title: Six questions, one freshness bound
messages.step.recap.lead: Ask what this caller needs before deciding whether a successful read can be used.
messages.visual.title: Revision Gap
messages.visual.eventualOk: revision 43 allowed by this weaker contract
messages.visual.noToken: without revision 44, the caller cannot state this lower bound
messages.visual.lowerBound: 44 ≥ 44, even if the source has reached 45
messages.rail.evidenceGap: The HTTP 200 read returned projected revision 43.
messages.rail.evidenceStrong: The caller carries a required minimum of 44.
messages.rail.evidenceControl: Projected revision 44 or 45 meets that minimum.
messages.rail.contractWeak: An ordinary projection read returns current projected state.
messages.rail.contractStrong: A successful minimum-revision read returns at least the requested revision.
messages.rail.contractEventual: This browsing read explicitly permits eventual data.
messages.rail.propertyHidden: Was this read fresh enough for this caller?
messages.rail.property: For requested minimum R, a successful result must have revision ≥ R.
messages.challenge.title: Does HTTP 200 satisfy this verification read?
messages.challenge.intro: The write returned committed revision 44. An asynchronous projection responds HTTP 200 with revision 43.
messages.challenge.question: What may the API claim under a minimum-revision-44 contract?
messages.option.reject: It cannot claim fresh-enough success with 43; wait, fall back, or return NOT_FRESH_ENOUGH.
messages.option.httpOk: HTTP 200 proves the projection has caught up to the write.
messages.option.sleep: A fixed sleep before reading proves revision 44 is visible.
messages.challenge.feedback: Revision 43 is below the caller's minimum 44. Transport success and arbitrary delay do not establish the requested freshness bound.
messages.deepDive.title: How does a read prove it is fresh enough?
messages.deepDive.section1.title: The successful stale read
messages.deepDive.section1.body: Nothing necessarily broke: the write committed at 44, the projection still had 43, and an ordinary read returned 43 with HTTP 200. The mismatch appears when verification needs at least 44.
messages.deepDive.section2.title: Carry the token end to end
messages.deepDive.section2.body: The write response gives the caller a lower-bound revision. The read request and every serving cache must enforce it. A system may wait, use an authoritative fallback, or explicitly decline.
messages.deepDive.section3.title: Minimum does not mean exact
messages.deepDive.section3.body: Projected revision 45 satisfies minimum 44, even if price changed again. Polling for price 120 or exactly revision 44 would reject a valid newer result.
messages.deepDive.section4.title: The useful weaker contract
messages.deepDive.section4.body: Browsing can explicitly accept eventual projected data with no minimum. Under that contract, revision 43 may be fine. The caller's workflow determines the required bound.
messages.deepDive.section5.title: The remaining limit
messages.deepDive.section5.body: A result at 44 proves only that it meets minimum 44. Revision 45 may already exist at the authority, so this contract does not establish absolute latest state.
messages.recap.1: Identity: which product did this read observe?
messages.recap.2: Authority: which write issued the committed revision?
messages.recap.3: Durability: did the write commit, and did the caller keep its token?
messages.recap.4: Delivery: how does the projection receive the new state?
messages.recap.5: Ordering: is projected revision at least the required revision?
messages.recap.6: Freshness: does this response meet this caller's lower bound?
